why-nextjs.title: Why We Choose Next.js For Every Project
why-nextjs.excerpt: Server-side rendering, SEO benefits, and development speed — why Next.js became our default choice.
content: Every time we start a new project, the first question is choosing the technology stack. Over the past three years, our answer has almost always been the same: Next.js.

The first reason is performance. Next.js's server-side rendering (SSR) and static generation (SSG) capabilities prepare pages on the server rather than in the client's browser. This significantly improves first-load speed and user experience.
The second reason is SEO. Google and other search engines prefer fully rendered HTML. Unlike client-side-only React apps, Next.js pages are served to search engines already rendered.
The third reason is development speed. File-based routing, built-in API routes, and image optimization let us focus on business logic instead of infrastructure.
Of course, not every project needs the same solution. But for web platforms, corporate sites, and SaaS products, Next.js remains our reliable choice.

mvp-for-startups.title: How to Build an MVP for a Startup: A Practical Guide
mvp-for-startups.excerpt: Core principles for building an MVP to reach the market quickly with limited budget and time.
content: Many startups try to make their first product fully featured and spend months, sometimes years, on it. This is one of the biggest mistakes.

A Minimal Viable Product (MVP) is the smallest version of a product that solves the customer's core problem without extra features. The goal is to test the idea with real users as quickly as possible.

In our experience, a successful MVP usually has three stages: first, clearly defining the core user problem; second, building the smallest feature set that solves it; third, iterating quickly based on real user feedback.
Technically, choosing a stack that enables rapid development matters for an MVP. Tools like Next.js, Supabase, or Firebase significantly cut the time spent building backend infrastructure.
Most importantly, an MVP doesn't need to be perfect. It's only meant to validate whether your idea is right, quickly and cheaply.

web-design-trends-2026.title: Web Design Trends to Expect in 2026
web-design-trends-2026.excerpt: Glassmorphism, 3D elements, and AI-powered personalized interfaces — design directions for the coming year.
content: Web design changes faster every year, and 2026 is no exception. Here are the key trends we're seeing while designing for our clients.
The first trend is the continued evolution of Glassmorphism. Transparent, blurred background effects are now used for more than decoration — they help visually clarify interface hierarchy.

The second trend is the growing popularity of 3D and interactive elements. Thanks to tools like Framer Motion and Three.js, adding complex 3D animations has become affordable and fast even for smaller projects.
The third trend is AI-powered personalization. Sites are starting to adapt content and interface in real time based on user behavior.

Finally, speed and minimalism remain the most important factor. No matter how beautiful a site is, a slow load loses the user. That's why we always aim to balance visual appeal with technical efficiency.

faq.title: Frequently Asked
faq.description: Find answers to the key questions you should know before starting your project.

items.question: How long does a project take to complete?
items.answer: A simple landing page takes 1-2 weeks, while a complex web platform or mobile app takes 4-8 weeks. The exact timeline is set once the technical specification (TS) is ready.

items.question: How is the project price determined?
items.answer: Price depends on project complexity, functionality, and timeline. We provide a free consultation and an exact quote for every project.

items.question: Is there technical support after the project is done?
items.answer: Yes, every project includes 24/7 technical support and free bug fixes for an agreed period.

items.question: What technologies do you use?
items.answer: We mainly use Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Node.js. Depending on project requirements, we also use Python, PostgreSQL, and other modern technologies.

items.question: Can you upgrade my existing website?
items.answer: Absolutely. We'll analyze your current project and prepare a proposal for migrating to modern technology or extending its functionality.

items.question: How does payment work?
items.answer: Projects are usually split into 2-3 stages, with payment made at the completion of each stage. Upfront payment terms are agreed at the start of the project.
